title: Rules-engine event
description: DESCRIPTIVE, NOT NORMATIVE. Generated from firmware source at FW 1.8.0 and re-verified field by field against FW 2.1.4 (branch fix/2.1.4, release commit "chore(release): 2.1.4", whose parent is x-nearest-commit). x-source line numbers are from the 1.8.0 generation and are STALE; fields added or changed for 2.1.4 cite functions instead. This is not a specification and not a proposal; it records what the device emits today. Plane: D2C telemetry. `required` lists only keys present in the minimal payload, i.e. those always emitted for this message type.

schema.description: Wire-contract identifier. Constant; bump signals a breaking payload change. Range/enum: Fixed literal "eflostop.v2".

ts.description: Device wall-clock when the message was built. Never below 1704067200 on the wire. Since 2.1.4 an event built before the first clock sync is not destroyed: it is held in the offline buffer and replayed after the first connect, with ts rewritten to the time the event happened, worked out from the hub uptime (the synced clock minus the uptime elapsed since gateway.uptime_s) and written into the buffer as soon as the clock first syncs. A pre-sync event still unstamped when the hub restarts (a restart before the clock synced) is dropped at replay, because its time cannot be known. Up to 2.1.3 every pre-sync event was destroyed, so a leak raised before the first sync was lost. Units: seconds (Unix epoch, UTC). Range/enum: >= 1704067200 (2024-01-01T00:00:00Z).
ts.x-source: build_envelope() / publish_json() main/telemetry/telemetry_v2.c; stamping ob_prepare_replay_locked() main/offline_buffer/offline_buffer.c; threshold EPOCH_VALID_THRESHOLD_TELEM

id.description: Immutable hub id derived from the WiFi STA MAC in eFuse. Same string used as the DPS registration id and the MQTT client id. Range/enum: "GW-" + 12 uppercase hex.

short_id.description: Last 2 bytes of the STA MAC as 4 hex chars. Also the SoftAP SSID suffix (WiFi-Hub-XXXX) the installer matches during setup. Range/enum: 4 uppercase hex chars.

name.description: User-assigned hub name from twin desired hub_name or C2D set_hub_name. NOTE the opposite convention on the twin plane, where hub_name is always emitted as "". Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars (HUB_NAME_MAX_LEN). Presence: conditional: OMITTED when the stored name is empty.

fw.description: Hub firmware version, read at runtime from the ESP-IDF app descriptor (PROJECT_VER). Never a hardcoded string. Range/enum: "2.1.4" for this release (CMakeLists.txt:12); "0.0.0" if the descriptor is empty.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since boot from the monotonic esp_timer. On an offline-buffer replay this is the ORIGINAL build-time value, possibly from a previous boot. For an event held from before the first clock sync (2.1.4) it is the uptime the replay used to work out ts. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0.

type.description: Envelope discriminator. Tells the backend which `data` shape to expect. Range/enum: enum: "lifecycle" | "snapshot" | "event".

event.description: Event discriminator inside data. The single most important routing key for the backend event log. Range/enum across the whole D2C plane, 16 values: online | valve_state_changed | leak_detected | leak_cleared | cmd_ack | auto_close | auto_close_blocked_override | auto_close_reenabled | rmleak_cleared | rmleak_auto_cleared | water_access_override_enabled | water_access_override_expired | device_offline | device_recovered | rules_engine | health_engine (valve_flood_detected / valve_flood_cleared were retired in 1.9.0). The enum below lists the values this message type carries. Presence: always in lifecycle and in every event shape; ABSENT in snapshot.

source_type.description: Which device detected the water that triggered the rule. Range/enum: ble_leak_sensor | lora | valve. Presence: auto_close (except the reconnect variant, which carries cause instead) and auto_close_blocked_override. NEVER on rmleak_cleared / rmleak_auto_cleared.

cause.description: Why a reconnect-variant auto_close fired: the valve reconnected with a leak still active. Replaces source_type on that variant (since 2.0.0). Range/enum: reconnect. Presence: reconnect auto_close only.

valve_id.description: The PROVISIONED valve's MAC (2.1.4: never the live link's). On auto_close / auto_close_blocked_override when the source is the valve; on rmleak_cleared / rmleak_auto_cleared always when it resolves. Range/enum: uppercase colon MAC. Presence: OMITTED when no valve is provisioned (or provisioning is busy); never a placeholder. A hub with no provisioned valve sends no auto_close at all (2.1.4).

sensor_id.description: The triggering sensor's id: "0x" + 8 uppercase hex (lora) or uppercase colon MAC (ble_leak_sensor). Presence: auto_close / auto_close_blocked_override when the source is a sensor.

rmleak_asserted.description: Whether the RMLEAK + close writes were actually issued to a reachable provisioned valve. false when the valve was unreachable (since 2.0.2; it was hardcoded true); since 2.1.4 the writes are then held for its reconnect, RMLEAK first. A hub with no provisioned valve sends no auto_close at all since 2.1.4 (up to 2.1.3 it sent one with false). Presence: auto_close only.

code.description: Machine-readable room code from the sensor_meta table; "unknown" when no metadata is stored. Range/enum: enum, 13 values.

label.description: User-entered free-text location label. Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars; "" when no metadata is stored.

location.description: Installed-location metadata for the triggering SENSOR. Presence: auto_close only; OMITTED for a valve source and when the sensor has no metadata (the opposite convention from leak events).

active_leak_count.description: How many sources were asserting a leak. Units: count. Presence: reconnect auto_close and water_access_override_expired only.

override_remaining_s.description: Seconds left in the override window. A window started before the clock synced is measured on the hub uptime until the clock syncs (2.1.4). Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0. A window with a real expiry restored after a power-on that lost the clock counts down from that power-on until the clock syncs (2.1.4; it used to be omitted). Presence: auto_close_blocked_override; OMITTED when the remaining time is unknown: the window has just expired but the rules tick has not processed it yet.

trigger.description: What opened the override window: a physical long-press on the valve, or the override_enable C2D command. Range/enum: enum: button | c2d_command. Presence: always (water_access_override_enabled only).

expires_ts.description: Absolute epoch at which the override window expires. Units: seconds (Unix epoch, UTC). Range/enum: >= 1704067200. Presence: water_access_override_enabled only, and OMITTED when the window was started before the clock synced (2.1.4; it used to carry an instant in 1970). The expiry is then about ts + remaining_s (ts is time-stamped at replay), and the snapshots carry expires_ts once the rules tick has re-based the window to the synced clock.

remaining_s.description: Full override window duration at the moment the window was started or refreshed. A CONSTANT, not a countdown; the countdown is override_remaining_s. Units: seconds. Range/enum: 86400 in a production build (compile-overridable via -D OVERRIDE_WINDOW_DURATION_S). Presence: always (water_access_override_enabled only).

override_cancelled.description: A leak_reset also tore down an open override window. Range/enum: always true when present. Presence: conditional: OMITTED when no override window was open.

previous_remaining_s.description: How much of the override window was discarded when it was cancelled early. A window started before the clock synced is measured on the hub uptime, and a window with a real expiry restored after a power-on that lost the clock counts down from that power-on until the clock syncs (2.1.4; both used to read 0). Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0. Presence: always (auto_close_reenabled only).

reason.description: Cause of the override cancellation on auto_close_reenabled. (A snapshot's data.reason is a different vocabulary.) Range/enum: c2d_command. Presence: auto_close_reenabled only.
reason.x-source: snapshot main/telemetry/telemetry_v2.c:383 with main/iothub/app_iothub.c:581-591 and :1570; rules event main/rules_engine/rules_engine.c:722

auto_close_resumed.description: Whether leaks were still active when the window expired, i.e. whether auto-close fired immediately on resume. Range/enum: true | false. Presence: always (water_access_override_expired only).

clear_after_seconds.description: The all-clear dwell time that had to elapse before the hub auto-cleared the RMLEAK interlock. Units: seconds. Range/enum: AUTO_CLEAR_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000. Presence: always (rmleak_auto_cleared only).

raw.description: Verbatim rules-/health-engine JSON string, emitted only when re-parsing that string fails. The string was itself produced by cJSON_PrintUnformatted, so this is reachable only on allocation failure. Presence: conditional: OMITTED unless cJSON_Parse of the engine JSON fails.

data.description: Rules-engine event (the engine's JSON becomes data), or the rules_engine fallback when it could not be re-parsed. Identity: valve_id or sensor_id per source, never both, never a placeholder.
